# RPC method success and refusal test coverage ratchet.
#
# Every line below is a gap the RPC door has today: a method in
# `src/rpc/method_class.rs` whose success answer or whose refusal is not
# asserted by a test in the coverage corpus (`src/rpc/tests.rs` and
# `src/tests/*.rs`). The ratchet in `rpc_every_method_has_success_and_refusal_test`
# reads this file in both directions: a line that is no longer missing fails the
# build until it is deleted, and a missing line that is not recorded here fails
# the build until a test is written. The file may therefore only shrink.
#
# These rows were invisible until now: the second loop of the ratchet compared
# the missing list against this file backwards, so no gap was ever reported and
# no line could ever be recorded. The rows are
# recorded, not excused: they close family by family, and every such
# change deletes the lines it closes.
#
# Closed families: the Solana compatibility surface (42 rows) is closed by
# `src/tests/rpc_door_solana.rs`. Six of those rows were the generated
# unsubscribe doors' `missing=refusal` halves, closed by a rule correction rather
# than a test: those doors are total, because jsonrpsee answers every
# unsubscribe call with `result: true/false` and never a JSON-RPC error, so no
# invalid call exists at this layer to refuse. `wants_refusal` in
# `src/rpc/method_class.rs` exempts them by name, sourced from the
# `unsubscribe = "..."` attributes of `src/rpc/api.rs`, and
# `rpc_door_solana::solana_unsubscribe_doors_answer_a_boolean_and_never_an_error`
# asserts that totality on the wire.
